And they went down and questioned the priest, and he said to them:
"Yes, she entered the church,
and when she saw that I was in the church,
she was ashamed before me,
and went out in haste,
without standing still at all."
And those faithful believed him as a priest.
And when they began to go around in the city
and to visit the houses of their relatives,
they saw the defiled pseudo-priest {OCR?} wearing boots,
and going out through the gate of the city.
And they seized him and brought him to the governor.
And when he scourged him a little,
he confessed,
and showed them her corpse, her ears, and her fingers.
And the whole city gathered there,
Arabs and Christians,
men and women,
and with great weeping and mournful dirges they brought her out and buried her.
And the defiled man they flayed and dismembered while alive,
and burned him.
And in the year one thousand four hundred and sixty-eight,
1468 of the Greeks [1157 AD], the Prince, lord of Antioch, entered Cyprus, which was [subject] to the Greeks,
and plundered the whole island:
people, sheep, cattle, horses, and all its wealth.
And when they brought them as far as the seashore,
the Cypriots paid a ransom for their lives and for their cattle with much gold,
and the Franks released them,
but took all the wealth.
And they also took the bishops, the heads of monasteries, and the chiefs of the people with them as hostages to Antioch,
until gold was paid [for them].
And in the year one thousand four hundred and sixty-nine,
1469 of the Greeks [1158 AD],
Stephan acted deceitfully against Thoros his brother,
and desired to kill him.
And when Thoros perceived it,
he seized him and imprisoned him for ten months.
And afterwards, at the persuasion of the Franks, he released him,
and he entered the service of the Franks.
And in that same year, which is the year five hundred and fifty-two,
552 of the Arabs [1157 AD],
there were severe earthquakes in Syria,
and they destroyed many places.
For Hama, its fortress and its city,
and all its courtyards collapsed upon old men, youths, and women,
and myriads of people perished in it.
And the fortress of Shaizar fell completely,
and no one escaped,
except for one woman and one eunuch alone.
And the people of Homs hastened and went outside and were saved,
but their houses perished together with its fortress.
And likewise the people of Aleppo fled and stayed outside for days and were saved,
and their houses were demolished,
and only five hundred souls perished in it.
And likewise in Kafartab and Apamea,
no one escaped.
